P1.evidence: No setter notes existed or were read back, and the rep did not know who was joining - 'I think I have a person with a different name who's supposed to be joining. Do you go by Alexander or Sascha?' The frame ran two of four parts: 'Really just want to understand what's going on with your fitness right now and what it is you're looking to accomplish', with nothing on obstacles or needs. Frame agreement was taken and given ('That sound good? Yeah'). The open question was never asked - the prospect simply started talking after the frame, so the rep got the information by luck rather than by asking.

P2.evidence: Age (21) and weight (85 kg to 90 kg and back to roughly 87.5 kg) were both volunteered, never asked; height was never established at all. Work was explored at length - med school, the web design business - but the desk-bound question was never put, and the fact that he sits all day came out only because he attributed his back pain to it. Health conditions were never asked as a question; every injury in a long list was volunteered. The injury check is the important one and it is genuinely split: the back pain was handled well, with a severity scale ('how bad is it like with the back pain? it like one to 10?') and a sleep follow-up, which is the best injury probing anywhere in this batch. But the current shin and femur fractures - disclosed while the prospect was physically wearing a brace on camera - got one question about how they happened and nothing about how long, healing status, restrictions, or whether anyone medical was managing them. Training week was covered thoroughly. Nutrition was asked directly ('How's your nutrition?') and followed up. Sleep and energy were touched only as a consequence of the back pain rather than asked in their own right.

P3.evidence: The deepest discovery in the batch, and the least converted. Mobility, strength and quality of muscle were explored properly, and the can't-do-right-now check landed on two concrete things: boxing, stopped for a year by his shoulder, and running while travelling without needing a gym. The bridge question was asked twice and the second version was excellent - 'Was there any moment that happened where you're like, okay, maybe just watching YouTube videos isn't going to cut it and now I need guidance?' - which produced the breakup, the reassessment and the faith motivation, all in the prospect's own words. From there it stalled. Nobody asked who else this impacts, even though he volunteered that he wants to 'motivate people also outside of the gym' and talked about proving something to his parents. The identity and legacy material arrived unprompted through faith - 'my body is the temple of the Holy Spirit' - and the rep acknowledged it but never drove it into a reflect-back. The summary at 00:21:42 was again a feature list: functional movement, saving travel time, working around injuries.

P4.evidence: The best-run phase on the call and the best P4 in the batch. Past attempts were established directly - 'have you reached out to anyone for any help around, you know, switching up your workouts, or maybe rehabbing your injuries' - producing 'it's my first time reaching out to somebody'. What happened with the self-directed approach was covered, and P4f ran in near-scripted form via the moment question, which is exactly the 'why can't you stick to it on your own' move in a better wrapper. The prospect named the gap himself and cleanly: 'I don't have the time or then want to spend my time searching for things... I want in sport, want somebody to guide me to health, to a perfect form. So that's what I'm looking for.' That is a prospect asking to be sold one-to-one coaching.

P5.evidence: Not run in any form - the fourth consecutive sales call in this batch with the entire 20-point Consequence Frame absent. The material here was unusually strong and the prospect handed it over himself: 'I'm 21, you know, I know something is wrong. I can't have these back pains with 21.' A two-year question aimed at a 21-year-old with nightly back pain, a fractured femur and a shoulder he has already had operated on writes itself. Not one of the four checks was attempted.

P6.evidence: No commitment check of any kind before presenting. Neither the belief question nor the all-in question was asked, and there was no clear yes to move forward on. The rep went from the mobility explanation straight to a budget question - 'like right now, like ballpark, like what do you have available to invest in your fitness' - which is an OC financial-picture move run out of sequence and before any value had been established or any commitment taken. That single question produced a self-declared $300 ceiling that the rest of the call was then priced against.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and no payment was collected. The prospect gave a clear verbal yes to Primal University - 'So I'm ready. Let's do it' - and the rep handed him a self-serve link in the Zoom chat rather than taking payment on the call. Onboarding with Trevor, the agreement email and the welcome sequence do not apply to the lower tier and were never reachable on the flagship.

objection_plays.detail: The most financial-picture work done anywhere in this batch, but run backwards. The rep did probe the money situation with real questions - 'are you saying that, like... All the money that you have went into the business, and it hasn't started getting clients yet, so therefore money is tight? Or what's going on with the money?' and 'Are they paying for your med school?' - which is two of the six financial picture areas. But he ran them before establishing value and before any commitment, and he never isolated ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%'), never used the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame, and never offered to break the payment up, which is the central move of the play. The only route to the flagship he raised was a credit card, delivered as an aside: 'Unless you had a credit card with like 10 grand that you want to just throw six of it onto this.' The prospect's constraint was explicitly temporary - 'as soon as I can afford it, I know I will do it' - which is the precise situation an instalment structure exists for.

Trigger was a stated scepticism about the authenticity of fitness figures on social media: 'nowadays social media, a lot of people are not genuine about what they do.' None of the OE moves ran - no 'would it be fair to say you're looking for certainty', no pleasure-versus-pain frame, no bridge or plane analogy, no 'how will you know if you never actually try'. The rep instead went into a tangent about the author David Hawkins and a psychology practice that grew by focusing on helping people. The objection dissolved only because the prospect talked himself out of it.
No think-about-it deferral. The prospect wanted to start immediately - 'I'm going to be honest with you, as soon as possible' - and the only barrier was cash.
No timing objection. He explicitly ruled timing out as the issue: 'It's not about time, it's not about if I want it, it's basically how much does it cost and when.'

No spousal consult. There is an adjacent situation - he refuses to ask his parents, who already pay 1,500 euros a month for his schooling - but he framed it as a decision he wants to own rather than permission he needs, so the OB trigger is absent.

Two unscripted situations, and the first is the most serious in the batch. There is no play, and no step anywhere in the process, for a prospect who discloses active fractures and a post-surgical shoulder. The known script gap has been recorded as a clinical-fit objection, but this call shows the gap is wider than that: here the prospect raised no clinical objection at all, so nothing in the script ever triggers, and an unsupervised programme is sold to someone in a leg brace. A clinical screening gate is needed independent of whether the prospect objects. Second: a prospect whose ceiling is $300 against a $6,000 offer, with high intent and a genuinely temporary constraint, and no mid-tier product and no instalment path to bridge it - the same missing tier a different prospect asked for by name two days earlier in this batch.

notes: Discovery was the strongest in the batch - P4 was genuinely well run and the prospect explicitly asked to be guided one-to-one - and it was then thrown away by asking for his budget before building any value, which capped the sale at his own $300 number. Two things to coach, in order. First and non-negotiable: when a prospect appears on camera in a brace and lists fractures, a shoulder operation and 6-7/10 nightly back pain, establish clinician clearance before discussing any programme, and do not place him in the unsupervised tier. Second: never ask what someone has available to invest before value is established and a commitment is taken.
